# Rule catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate.py from the rules and scenarios. Do not edit. -->

16 rules. Framework versions: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025; OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026; MITRE ATLAS 2026.09; MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise 19.2.

**Telemetry** states what a rule needs beyond event metadata: *Content detector* rules read a field that an upstream detector derives from prompts or responses; *Raw content* rules search the prompt or response text itself. A framework mapping records which risk a rule relates to; it is not a claim of complete coverage.

## Agent tool abuse

<a id="tool-call-amplification-loop"></a>
### High Tool-Call Volume in One Conversation

Detects fifteen or more tool calls or sub-agent invocations within one conversation in a fixed 2-minute window. A runaway or coerced agent that fans out or loops consumes API budget and downstream capacity with every call. The threshold is a starting point; baseline the normal fan-out of each agent before enabling alerts.

| | |
|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/agent_tool_abuse/tool_call_amplification_loop.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/agent_tool_abuse/tool_call_amplification_loop.yml) · `1d6f3b08-9c47-4a2e-8b51-5e2a7c0d9f84` |
| Level | medium |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | >= 15 matching events per `user.tenant.id`, `gen_ai.conversation.id` in a fixed 2-minute UTC window |
| Fields | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, `user.tenant.id` |
| Telemetry | Metadata only |
| Mappings | LLM10 Unbounded Consumption<br>LLM06 Excessive Agency<br>ASI02 Tool Misuse and Exploitation<br>[AML.T0034.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034.002) Cost Harvesting: Agentic Resource Consumption |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/agent_tool_abuse/tool_call_amplification_loop.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/agent_tool_abuse/tool_call_amplification_loop.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/agent_tool_abuse/tool_call_amplification_loop.yml) (5 cases) |

False positives:

- Research, planning or data-pipeline agents whose normal turns fan out across many tools; scope by gen_ai.agent.name or raise the threshold.
- Batch jobs that drive many tool calls under one conversation.

<a id="denied-tool-retry-loop"></a>
### Repeated Denied Tool Calls in One Conversation

Detects three or more denied tool calls within one conversation in a fixed 5-minute window. An agent that keeps invoking tools its policy refuses is probing for a path around the policy, often because injected instructions are steering it. One denial is routine; repetition is the signal.

| Telemetry | Metadata only |
| Mappings | LLM06 Excessive Agency<br>ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse<br>[AML.T0053](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0053) AI Agent Tool Invocation |

False positives:

- An agent retrying a tool that is out of scope for the tenant; grant or document the scope.
- Transient authorization failures reported as denied during an outage; correlate with error.type.
- Authorized agent-evaluation suites that probe tool boundaries.

<a id="anomalous-tool-call-chain"></a>
### Sensitive-Read and Egress Tools in One Agent Tool Chain

Detects an agent tool chain that includes both a tool that reads sensitive data (files, databases, secrets, mailboxes) and a tool that sends data out (email, HTTP, webhooks, uploads). The combination is the shape of data exfiltration through agent tools. The rule tests co-occurrence only: it does not see call order, arguments, destinations or authorization. Tool names must match exactly (case-insensitively); replace the lists with your application's tool inventory, including namespaces.

| Level | medium |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | Single event |
| Fields | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `tool.call.chain` |
| Telemetry | Metadata only |
| Mappings | LLM06 Excessive Agency<br>ASI02 Tool Misuse and Exploitation<br>[AML.T0086](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0086) Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation<br>[AML.T0085.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0085.001) Data from AI Services: AI Agent Tools |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/agent_tool_abuse/anomalous_tool_call_chain.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/agent_tool_abuse/anomalous_tool_call_chain.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/agent_tool_abuse/anomalous_tool_call_chain.yml) (7 cases) |

False positives:

- Automation that reads internal data and notifies an external channel by design, such as posting a database status to Slack; scope by gen_ai.agent.name or allowlist the chain.
- Synchronization agents whose normal job is to read in one place and write in another.

## Data exfiltration

<a id="pii-secret-exfiltration-in-output"></a>
### Repeated Sensitive Data in LLM Output for One Principal

Detects five or more responses labeled with personal-data or credential classes for one principal within a fixed 10-minute window. A single sensitive response can be legitimate; repeated ones for the same principal indicate data being harvested through the model. The rule reads the detector's class labels, never the sensitive values.

| | |
|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/data_exfiltration/pii_secret_exfiltration_in_output.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/data_exfiltration/pii_secret_exfiltration_in_output.yml) · `5003fb2c-aa74-4b96-a00a-59a5792c5de1` |
| Level | high |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | >= 5 matching events per `user.tenant.id`, `user.id` in a fixed 10-minute UTC window |
| Fields | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `user.id`, `user.tenant.id`, `content.output.pii.types`, `content.output.secret.types` |
| Telemetry | Content detector |
| Mappings | LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure<br>[AML.T0057](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0057) LLM Data Leakage |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/data_exfiltration/pii_secret_exfiltration_in_output.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/data_exfiltration/pii_secret_exfiltration_in_output.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/data_exfiltration/pii_secret_exfiltration_in_output.yml) (6 cases) |

False positives:

- Assistants that return customer records by design, such as HR, CRM or support copilots; scope by service.name or user.roles.
- Export or reporting jobs that run under one service principal.
- An over-eager classifier that labels benign tokens, for example any number as a phone number.

## Dos cost abuse

<a id="request-rate-burst-per-principal"></a>
### Completion Request Burst from One Principal

Detects twenty or more completion requests from one principal within a fixed 1-minute window, regardless of request size. High request frequency from a single identity degrades service for other users and raises cost. Set the threshold above the rate of each application's heaviest legitimate client.

|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/dos_cost_abuse/request_rate_burst_per_principal.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/dos_cost_abuse/request_rate_burst_per_principal.yml) · `c399339c-8147-4dff-92c6-16588e7c92c7` |
| Level | medium |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | >= 20 matching events per `user.tenant.id`, `user.id` in a fixed 1-minute UTC window |
| Fields | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `user.id`, `user.tenant.id` |
| Telemetry | Metadata only |
| Mappings | LLM10 Unbounded Consumption<br>[AML.T0034.000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034.000) Cost Harvesting: Excessive Queries<br>[AML.T0029](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0029) Denial of AI Service |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/dos_cost_abuse/request_rate_burst_per_principal.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/dos_cost_abuse/request_rate_burst_per_principal.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/dos_cost_abuse/request_rate_burst_per_principal.yml) (5 cases) |

False positives:

- High-throughput service principals, evaluation harnesses or synthetic monitoring; scope by user.roles or raise the threshold.
- Clients retrying during an error storm; correlate with error.type.
- Load tests; filter by deployment.environment.name.

<a id="token-cost-spike-per-principal"></a>
### Repeated High-Token Completions for One Principal

Detects ten or more completions of 8,000 tokens or more for one principal within a fixed 5-minute window. Sustained resource-intensive requests from one identity drive up cost (denial of wallet) and consume shared capacity. Both thresholds are starting points; set them from each application's normal usage.

| Telemetry | Metadata only |

False positives:

- Batch or backfill jobs under one service principal; scope by user.roles or raise the threshold for known principals.

<a id="repeated-length-finish-loops"></a>
### Repeated Length-Truncated Completions in One Conversation

Detects five or more completions that hit their output-token limit within one conversation in a fixed 5-minute window. An agent or auto-continue loop that keeps exhausting its output budget without converging burns tokens on every turn. Legitimate long-form generation also produces this pattern, so treat it as a hunting signal.

| Level | low |

| Logic | >= 5 matching events per `user.tenant.id`, `gen_ai.conversation.id` in a fixed 5-minute UTC window |
| Fields | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, `user.tenant.id`, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` |
| Telemetry | Metadata only |
| Mappings | LLM10 Unbounded Consumption<br>[AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/dos_cost_abuse/repeated_length_finish_loops.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/dos_cost_abuse/repeated_length_finish_loops.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/dos_cost_abuse/repeated_length_finish_loops.yml) (4 cases) |

False positives:

- Clients that deliberately continue long outputs across several capped turns.
- Summarization or translation of large documents split into capped chunks.

<a id="oversized-max-tokens"></a>
### Very Large Output Budget Requested

Detects a completion request whose max_tokens is 100,000 or more. Requests for very long outputs are a direct lever on cost and latency. Some current models accept output budgets of this size legitimately, so this is a governance signal: set the threshold just above the largest budget each application is expected to request.

| Level | low |

| Telemetry | Metadata only |

## Insecure output

<a id="unsanitized-output-to-sink"></a>
### Unsanitized LLM Output Reached an Interpreter or Renderer

Detects model output that reached a SQL, shell, code-evaluation or HTML sink without sanitization, as reported by the application's output-handling instrumentation. Output treated as trusted by an interpreter is how prompt injection becomes SQL injection, command execution or cross-site scripting. Markdown sinks are excluded because unsanitized Markdown rendering is usually a standing configuration issue rather than an event; audit it separately.

| | |
|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/insecure_output/unsanitized_output_to_sink.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/insecure_output/unsanitized_output_to_sink.yml) · `3bc7ddec-e008-450b-950c-263f73f90440` |
| Level | high |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | Single event |
| Fields | `output.sink`, `output.rendered_unsanitized` |
| Telemetry | Metadata only |
| Mappings | LLM05 Improper Output Handling<br>ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution<br>[T1059](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/) Command and Scripting Interpreter |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/insecure_output/unsanitized_output_to_sink.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/insecure_output/unsanitized_output_to_sink.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/insecure_output/unsanitized_output_to_sink.yml) (6 cases) |

False positives:

- Consumers that sanitize or escape output after the point where the instrumentation records it; confirm the downstream control before dismissing.
- Internal tools that evaluate trusted, templated output in a sandbox; scope by service.name.

## Jailbreak

<a id="persona-safety-bypass-loop"></a>
### Repeated Blocked Jailbreak Attempts in One Conversation

Detects three or more content-filtered jailbreak attempts within one conversation in a fixed 10-minute window. Repetition distinguishes an adversary iterating on persona or safety-bypass framings from a single blocked request. Every counted attempt was blocked; look for an unfiltered response later in the same conversation to judge whether one succeeded.

|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/jailbreak/persona_safety_bypass_loop.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/jailbreak/persona_safety_bypass_loop.yml) · `413f181a-a47a-4213-ba58-0768307ec9dc` |
| Level | medium |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | >= 3 matching events per `user.tenant.id`, `gen_ai.conversation.id` in a fixed 10-minute UTC window |
| Fields | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, `user.tenant.id`, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, `gen_ai.input.messages` |
| Telemetry | Raw content |
| Mappings | LLM01 Prompt Injection<br>[AML.T0054](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0054) LLM Jailbreak |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/jailbreak/persona_safety_bypass_loop.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/jailbreak/persona_safety_bypass_loop.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/jailbreak/persona_safety_bypass_loop.yml) (6 cases) |

False positives:

- Authorized red-team or safety-evaluation suites probing the content filter in one session.
- A user rephrasing a benign request that an over-sensitive content filter keeps blocking.

## Prompt injection

<a id="indirect-injection-from-untrusted-source"></a>
### Injection Phrase in Retrieval-Augmented Input from Untrusted Sources

Detects an instruction-override phrase in the input of an operation that retrieved content from an untrusted source type (web, email, file or ticket), when the injection-marker detector also scored the input. This is the log signature of indirect prompt injection, where instructions planted in retrieved content reach the model's context. The rule cannot tell which message carried the phrase: a user who types it during a retrieval-augmented session also matches.

| | |
|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/prompt_injection/indirect_injection_from_untrusted_source.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/prompt_injection/indirect_injection_from_untrusted_source.yml) · `fac11223-21c0-48f6-afcb-bdc6a7ac630f` |
| Level | medium |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | Single event |
| Fields | `rag.source.types`, `gen_ai.input.messages`, `content.input.injection_markers` |
| Telemetry | Raw content |
| Mappings | LLM01 Prompt Injection<br>[AML.T0051.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.001) LLM Prompt Injection: Indirect |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/prompt_injection/indirect_injection_from_untrusted_source.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/prompt_injection/indirect_injection_from_untrusted_source.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/prompt_injection/indirect_injection_from_untrusted_source.yml) (6 cases) |

False positives:

- Retrieved documents that quote injection phrases legitimately, such as security advisories or abuse reports.
- Trusted sources labeled web or file by an over-broad source classifier; correct the labeling upstream.
- Users who type an override phrase themselves while retrieval is active.

<a id="direct-injection-markers"></a>
### Instruction-Override Phrase in LLM Input

Detects an input message that contains a common instruction-override phrase, such as "ignore previous instructions", when the gateway's injection-marker detector also scored the input. This indicates a direct prompt-injection attempt; it does not show that the model followed the injected instruction. Phrase matching is English-only and easy to evade, so treat an alert as a lead rather than a verdict.

| Rule | [`rules/prompt_injection/direct_injection_markers.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/prompt_injection/direct_injection_markers.yml) · `cc0cd2b6-0ef0-4782-99aa-a84c006b32c6` |
| Level | medium |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | Single event |
| Fields | `gen_ai.input.messages`, `content.input.injection_markers` |
| Telemetry | Raw content |
| Mappings | LLM01 Prompt Injection<br>[AML.T0051.000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.000) LLM Prompt Injection: Direct |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/prompt_injection/direct_injection_markers.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/prompt_injection/direct_injection_markers.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/prompt_injection/direct_injection_markers.yml) (5 cases) |

False positives:

- Authorized red-team or regression testing of the application's own defenses.
- Users quoting or discussing injection phrases, for example in a support request about the assistant, when the marker detector also scores the input.

<a id="direct-injection-marker-count"></a>
### Multiple Injection Markers Scored on LLM Input

Detects an input that the gateway's injection-marker detector scored with two or more prompt-injection or instruction-extraction markers. The rule reads only the derived marker count, so it runs without storing prompt text; its precision is the precision of the upstream detector. Pair it with the phrase-based rule where content logging is enabled.

- Authorized red-team or regression suites that submit injection-rich inputs.

## System prompt extraction

<a id="system-prompt-disclosure-phrases"></a>
### Instruction-Disclosure Phrase in LLM Output

Detects a response containing a phrase that commonly introduces recited instructions, such as "my system prompt" or "here are my instructions". It is a hunting signal for deployments without an output detector: the phrases also appear when an assistant talks about prompts in general, and a response can disclose instructions without them.

|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_disclosure_phrases.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_disclosure_phrases.yml) · `7d0f4c5e-2b8a-4d63-9e1f-3a6c5b8e2d14` |
| Level | low |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | Single event |
| Fields | `gen_ai.output.messages` |
| Telemetry | Raw content |
| Mappings | LLM07 System Prompt Leakage<br>[AML.T0056](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0056) Extract LLM System Prompt |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_disclosure_phrases.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_disclosure_phrases.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_disclosure_phrases.yml) (4 cases) |

False positives:

- Responses that discuss prompt engineering or quote a generic instruction such as "you are a helpful assistant".
- Assistants that describe their intended behavior on request, by design.

<a id="system-prompt-leaked-in-output"></a>
### System-Prompt Content Detected in LLM Output

Detects a response in which the gateway's output detector found content from the application's system instructions, for example through a canary token or similarity check. The rule reads only the derived flag, so it runs without storing response text. Review the response against the application's disclosure policy: some deployments intentionally reveal part of their instructions.

| Rule | [`rules/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_leaked_in_output.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_leaked_in_output.yml) · `05450153-9a94-4bbb-bae5-c9ba47c92f4f` |
| Level | high |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | Single event |
| Fields | `content.output.contains_system_prompt` |
| Telemetry | Content detector |
| Mappings | LLM07 System Prompt Leakage<br>[AML.T0056](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0056) Extract LLM System Prompt |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_leaked_in_output.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_leaked_in_output.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/system_prompt_extraction/system_prompt_leaked_in_output.yml) (3 cases) |

False positives:

- Assistants that intentionally disclose a public portion of their instructions, such as a documented persona.
- Detector false positives on short or generic instruction text; prefer canary-token checks where possible.

<a id="extract-system-prompt-markers"></a>
### System-Prompt Extraction Phrase in LLM Input

Detects an input message that asks for the application's system prompt or hidden instructions, such as "print your system prompt" or "repeat the words above", when the injection-marker detector also scored the input. This indicates an extraction attempt; the companion output rules indicate whether instructions were disclosed. Generic instruction-override phrases are left to the prompt-injection rules.

|---|---|
| Rule | [`rules/system_prompt_extraction/extract_system_prompt_markers.yml`](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/rules/system_prompt_extraction/extract_system_prompt_markers.yml) · `206aa5bc-49a1-439e-a0ba-f4e11298643d` |
| Level | medium |
| Status | experimental |
| Logic | Single event |
| Fields | `gen_ai.input.messages`, `content.input.injection_markers` |
| Telemetry | Raw content |
| Mappings | LLM07 System Prompt Leakage<br>[AML.T0056](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0056) Extract LLM System Prompt |
| Queries | [SPL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/splunk/system_prompt_extraction/extract_system_prompt_markers.spl) · [KQL](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/siem/sentinel/system_prompt_extraction/extract_system_prompt_markers.kql) · [scenarios](https://github.com/NotACop38/PromptHound/blob/main/scenarios/system_prompt_extraction/extract_system_prompt_markers.yml) (4 cases) |

False positives:

- Developers or red teams inspecting their own application's prompt during authorized testing.
- Users who ask about the assistant's instructions out of curiosity when the marker detector also scores the question.
